The Water Cycle
Water on Earth is always moving. The sun heats water in oceans, lakes and rivers, and it evaporates into water vapor. As the vapor rises it cools and condenses into tiny droplets that form clouds. When the droplets combine and grow heavy, they fall back to the ground as precipitation: rain, snow, sleet or hail. Some of that water soaks into the soil as groundwater, and some runs off into streams and back to the ocean, where the cycle begins again. Plants also release water vapor through their leaves in a process called transpiration.
